source.title: Ghosts of Softmax: Complex Singularities That Limit Safe Step Sizes in Cross-Entropy

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or document mismatch.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own cross-entropy step-stability experiments, but does not test whether gradient-based training reaches near-zero training classification error, the local-minima, depth, initialization, or normalization claims, or the squared-loss and sharpness behavior specified in V5. Its cited discussion of those studies is prior work, not a result of this paper.
record.gate_note: The paper measures loss inflation, prediction changes, and test accuracy under step-size sweeps and training recipes. These are relevant optimization-stability findings, but they do not measure the training-error outcome or the specific conditions named by V1–V6. Cited catapult and edge-of-stability results are not this paper's own results.
record.test_reason: The study measures cross-entropy step hazards and controller performance, not an outcome specified by V1–V6. Its radius ρa is distinct from V5's initial linearized-model learning-rate threshold and Hessian sharpness threshold. Appendix 5 reports directional-curvature comparisons and a margin–learning-rate relationship, but does not measure catapult recovery with falling curvature, sharpness hovering at 2/η during full-batch training, or divergence from below that threshold. The related-work discussion cites those phenomena without testing them.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors attribute cross-entropy Taylor-radius constraints to complex partition-function zeros and report that a computable linearized-logit proxy predicts update hazards and enables a useful controller in their experiments. They distinguish one-step reliability from global convergence, acknowledge confidence-margin slack and nonlinear-logit approximation error, and leave larger-scale validation open. The proxy is not an unconditional safety guarantee for nonlinear networks.
record.recipe_differences: The experiments study cross-entropy stability using radius-normalized step sweeps, learning-rate spikes, and an adaptive controller. They do not reproduce the benchmark training-error measurements in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary with learning rate and spike size, architecture, update direction, temperature normalization, and controller target r. In ResNet18/CIFAR-10, fixed learning rates show different accuracy and violation counts; at 10 000× spikes, architecture and method change final test accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Cross-entropy spike tests and 10-epoch ResNet-18/CIFAR-10 runs relate instability to r = τ/ρa. The proposed controller survives tested spikes and reaches 85.3% test accuracy at target r = 1 versus 82.6% for the best tested fixed rate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A direction-dependent, linearized-logit radius estimate can diagnose and mitigate some cross-entropy update failures in the tested settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix 5 reports directional Hessian scales exceeding ρa across 20 random directions at three training stages, with the discrepancy increasing from approximately 10× to 460×. It also reports a crossover-margin relationship with log learning rate and R² approximately 1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the reported cross-entropy experiments, directional curvature scales and the proposed Taylor-radius diagnostic differ substantially; these comparisons do not establish edge-of-stability training dynamics.

record.problems: Experiments are small-scale; ResNet-18/CIFAR-10 training is limited to 10 epochs, with longer runs left for future work. The paper says the radius is conservative and linearization may be inaccurate when logits curve over a step. Mini-batch estimates are approximate. Several results are shown in figures with medians and IQR bands rather than exact per-seed values.
record.rows_left_out: Not applicable; 20 rows retained, below the 60-row limit. Single-step six-architecture sweeps, random-direction and temperature-scaling outcomes, and the tiny-transformer artifact were not extracted as rows because they are not measurements of the claim versions' specified training-error outcomes; their reported summary findings do not supply evidence for V1–V6.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error in sufficiently large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, and model-size or training-recipe qualifications.
Spurious local minima in realizable two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and their reduction through student overparameterization.
Training-error degradation with plain-network depth, prevention by identity shortcuts, and the special-initialization and normalization-free exceptions.
Initialization effects on signal propagation, training speed and trainable depth, including orthogonal versus Gaussian weights.

Squared-loss catapult recovery above the initial linearized stability limit with curvature reduction; full-batch sharpness hovering at 2/η while loss falls; divergence despite starting below that threshold.
Matched BatchNorm versus no-BatchNorm training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup's normalization-free training comparison.

record.verdict_notes: All rows remain linked to none; cannot_determine denotes their inability to establish a version's effect, not unreadable reported values. The omitted single-step, temperature and tiny-transformer experiments are already declared in rows_left_out. Appendix 5's additional empirical assertions fit no version and do not require a missing claim-evidence row.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted or random labels; effects of model size, early stopping, and regularization.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student local minima and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual network training error across depth; special initialization and normalization-free residual training.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, and 10,000-layer training.

Squared-loss recovery above the initial linearized stability limit, sharpness hovering at the stability threshold, and divergence starting below that threshold. The paper instead studies cross-entropy step-radius stability.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup training without normalization.
